[[Gota Yashiki]] }} '''Plastics''', or '''the Plastics''', were a short-lived Japanese [[New wave music|new wave]] band who rose to prominence in the late 1970s and early 1980s.{{cite web|url=https://neojaponisme.com/2016/03/01/the-plastics-and-copy-anxiety/|title=The Plastics and Copy Anxiety|last=Marx|first=W. David|website=Neojaponisme|accessdate=9 April 2016}} originally issue #4 Audimat (in French). Their music was a major influence on Japanese pop music and their songs have been covered by many bands, most notably [[Polysics]], [[Pizzicato Five]], and [[Stereo Total]]. In September 2007, ''[[Rolling Stone|Rolling Stone Japan]]'' ranked their debut album ''Welcome Plastics'' at No. 19 on their list of the "100 Greatest Japanese Rock Albums of All Time".{{cite web |title=English translation and summary of the ''Rolling Stone Japan'' article |website=Neojaponisme.com |url=https://neojaponisme.com/2007/11/09/100-greatest-japanese-rock-albums/ |accessdate=2011-12-11}} == Biography == Fellow new wave bands [[Talking Heads]], [[The B-52's]] and [[Devo]] were fans of Plastics and were instrumental in getting their albums released in the United States. The band's mainstream exposure began when [[Toshio Nakanishi]] designed a tour program book for Talking Heads and gave their frontman [[David Byrne (musician)|David Byrne]] a tape of Plastics demos. Byrne promptly sent it to the B-52's' manager, who offered to represent them internationally.{{Cite web|url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/masahide_sakuma_of_plastics_dies_at_61|title=Masahide Sakuma of the Plastics Dies at 61|website=Exclaim.ca|accessdate=3 October 2020}} The band used the [[Roland Corporation|Roland]] CR-68 and [[Roland CR-78|CR-78]] [[drum machine]]s for their early albums. In 1980, member [[:ja:佐久間正英|Masahide Sakuma]] had some input on the Roland Corporation's development of the [[Roland TR-808]] drum machine. When its development was complete, the Plastics owned the first TR-808 model, which they used on their 1981 album ''Welcome Back''.Masahide Sakuma, [http://masahidesakuma.net/2012/04/roland-tr808.html ROLAND TR-808の記憶] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140209073400/http://masahidesakuma.net/2012/04/roland-tr808.html |date=2014-02-09 }}, April 5, 2012 On February 19, 1982, [[NBC]]'s late night comedy show ''[[Second City Television|SCTV]]'' aired the promotional video for Plastics' song "Top Secret Man" as part of the "Midnight Video Special" sketch, hosted by Gerry Todd ([[Rick Moranis]]).{{Cite web|url=http://sctvguide.ca/episodes/sctv_s42.htm#Show_9|title=SCTV Guide - Episodes - Series 4 Cycle 2|website=Sctvguide.ca|accessdate=3 October 2020}} [[Stereo Total]]'s cover of their song "[[I Love You, Oh No|I Love You, Oh No!]]" (with the title amended to "I Love You Ono") was used in television commercials for [[Sony Mobile|Sony Ericsson]] in Europe around 2006 and by [[Dell]] computers in the US in 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.advertolog.com/dell/adverts/discovery-13187655/|title=Discovery Dell TV Commercial Ad|website=Advertlog.com}} On January 16, 2014, Masahide Sakuma died from scirrhous gastric cancer and a brain tumor. He was 61. On May 10, 2016, Plastics got together to perform their final concert at [[Blue Note Tokyo]]. On February 25, 2017, Toshio Nakanishi died from esophageal cancer, also at the age of 61. The following year, the band released the recording of their final concert under the name ''A'' in memory of Nakanishi.{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/7702186/plastics-major-force-co-creator-toshio-nakanishi-obit|title=Plastics Artist and Major Force Co-Creator Toshio Nakanishi Dies at 61 |website=Billboard.com|accessdate=3 October 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pollstar.com/article/plastics-leader-nakanishi-dies-130893|title=Plastics Leader Nakanishi Dies|website=Pollstar.com|accessdate=3 October 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.slogan.co.jp/portfolio/plastics-a/|title=PLASTICS -A|website=Slogan|access-date=1 May 2022}} == Band members == * {{Nihongo|[[Chica Sato]]|佐藤　チカ}} – vocal, synth drums * {{Nihongo|[[Toshio Nakanishi]]|中西　俊夫}} – vocal, guitar & percussion * {{Nihongo|[[:ja:立花ハジメ|Hajime Tachibana]]|立花　{{ruby|肇|ハジメ}}}} – guitar & vocal * {{Nihongo|[[:ja:佐久間正英|Masahide Sakuma]]|佐久間　正英}} – keyboards, guitar & bass programming * {{Nihongo|[[:ja:島武実|Takemi Shima]]|島　武実}} – rhythm box == Discography == === Studio albums === {|class="wikitable" ! style="width:33px;"|Year ! style="width:300px;"|Title ! In September 2007, Rolling Stone Japan ranked their debut album Welcome Plastics at No. 19 on their list of the "100 Greatest Japanese Rock Albums of All Time".
